## Why this site

This site collects my self-study notes in engineering, built from the open courses of [MIT OpenCourseWare](https://ocw.mit.edu). It has three goals:

- **Consolidate what I learn.** Writing up and rephrasing each lecture in my own words is where understanding is really tested.
- **Keep tangible evidence** of this work, in particular toward a VAE (*Validation des Acquis de l'Expérience*, a French accreditation of prior experiential learning).
- **Show that the understanding is operational**, not just theoretical — each note comes with Python demonstrations (numerical checks, visualizations).

## The method

I learn with the **Feynman method**: until I can re-explain a concept simply, I haven't understood it. Each note follows three stages — theoretical **discovery**, **practice**, then **metacognition** (re-explaining, spotting the pitfalls).

Concretely, every note shares the same template: *In brief → Concepts → Key intuition → Python demonstration → Feynman test → Pitfalls.*

## The courses

### Available

- **[18.02 — Multivariable Calculus](courses/18.02/index.qmd)**
  Vectors and matrices, partial derivatives, multiple integrals, Green's and Stokes' theorems.
  *(Course completed; notes being published.)*

### Roadmap

My path follows an order meant so that each course prepares the next — and all of them have **video lectures**, to support the discovery stage:

1. **8.01SC** — Classical Mechanics *(Newtonian mechanics: the bedrock of engineering physics)*
2. **18.03** — Differential Equations *(modeling how systems evolve over time)*
3. **18.06** — Linear Algebra *(the language of matrices, everywhere in engineering and data science)*
4. **8.02** — Electricity & Magnetism *(electric and magnetic fields, Maxwell's equations)*
5. **2.003SC** — Engineering Dynamics *(dynamics and vibrations of mechanical systems)*
6. **16.01** — Unified Engineering *(an integrated introduction to aerospace engineering)*
